newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh taka ends marginally weaker.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh taka ends marginally weaker.

text.p: Easing of call rates pushed the Bangladesh taka marginally down to close at 42.8250/8350 to the dollar in interbank trading on Sunday, dealers said.
The local unit opened steady at 42.8150/8350 per dollar in early trade but lost ground on a shrinking dollar supply.
One dealer said initially purchases of dollars by a large private bank strained the local currency. "Also banks opted to hold back dollars due to weakening of the call rates," he said.
Interbank call money rates finished at 5.0 to 6.5 percent against the previous 5.75-6.75 percent.
